propositions: The CLI write commands use hand-rolled argument-parsing loops that are difficult to maintain and drift from schema; the refactor must retire these loops in favor of stdlib argparse while preserving all observable behavior.

The --assignee flag must distinguish between absent (triggers default_assignee fallback, None sentinel), empty string explicit clear, and value-less error exit; --force must support bare form (consuming following non-option token in claim, not in transition) and --force=reason inline form with different semantics per command.

The transition._parse_flags function is called directly by three external tests and must remain a thin shim returning the identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) with None-vs-empty-string distinctions intact; the retired --force-close flag must reject with exit code 1 and historical message.

Unknown/extra CLI tokens must be silently skipped, --help must remain dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden help files (not regenerated by argparse), prefix abbreviation must be disabled, and error messages for value-less flags must exit 1 with existing wording not argparse's exit-2 + usage.

The refactor reduced transition._parse_flags complexity below the configured threshold, requiring .github/complexity-baseline.json to drain the stale entry to pass the complexity-baseline test and satisfy the ratchet enforcement.

Gerrit change 1886 is dual-green (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1 from CI) with all 674 lifecycle/unit tests passing, make lint and make typecheck green, and module-size/complexity ratchets respected; awaiting operator submission go-ahead.
